The Challenge

Plenty of sales data, no clear picture of who performs

Clix's lending business sells Business Loans, Loans Against Property, K12 school finance and direct-to-consumer products across five regions. Performance lived in separate, inconsistent files, so every review started with an argument about the numbers.

Unclear performance

No structured way to tell high performers from non-performers, or how close the middle was to the line.

Data quality issues

Fragmented, unclean and inconsistent sales data across sources, with the same value spelt five ways.

No single view

No single source of truth and no visual dashboards, so decisions leaned on whoever had the latest file.

Hidden hotspots

Region-level averages hid where productivity was really failing: specific products in specific regions.

HMC Approach

Clean it, cut it, model it, show it

Built with Clix's sales leadership, from raw extracts to an insight pack they could take into regional reviews.

Select a step to see what happened.

Discover · Agree what "performer" means

Before any analysis, the business agreed one definition.

  • Performer: at or above 50% of target; a separate tier for 100%+.
  • Potential performer: close enough to the line to be converted.
  • Cuts that matter: region, designation, age category, product.

Deliverable: Performance definitions and data inventory.

Clean · One reliable dataset

Excel and Power Query, then Python for the last mile.

  • Trimmed, de-duplicated and standardised every categorical column.
  • Unified the performer label variants into one value.
  • Flagged outliers rather than silently dropping them.

Deliverable: Clean analysis dataset and data-quality log.

Analyse · Segments, trends, models

Python for segmentation, trend detection and outlier identification.

  • Region × product breakdown of performers and non-performers.
  • Hierarchical tiers with a conversion view of potential performers.
  • Random forest and logistic regression compared on the same split.

Deliverable: Insight pack and model notebook.

Adopt · Targeted interventions

Insights went straight into regional reviews.

  • Potential performers named and coached first.
  • North and LAP flagged for structural fixes.
  • West Business Loan practices documented for others to copy.

Deliverable: Intervention list by region and product.

Scale · Repeat every quarter

The same pipeline reruns on new data.

  • Cleaning rules saved as reusable functions.
  • Tiers and conversion tracked quarter on quarter.
  • Model retrained as more history builds up.

Deliverable: Reusable pipeline and dashboard template.
